async def choose_material(req: EffectiveRequirement, research: RequirementResearch,
                          materials: dict[str, MaterialRecord], trace: Trace | None = None
                          ) -> tuple[str | None, list[str]]:
    """The model picks the material from the inspected candidates; `evidence.check_choice` validates the exact
    match and status and sends a wrong choice back with the reason."""
    if req.stroke is None:
        return None, [f"{req.requirement_id}: stroke pending ({'; '.join(req.pending)})"]
    if not materials:
        return None, [f"{req.requirement_id}: no material could be inspected"]
    agent = Agent(llm.model(), output_type=MaterialChoice, instructions=CHOOSE_MATERIAL,
                  model_settings=llm.settings(CHOOSE_THINKING, timeout=llm.env_seconds("LLM_CHOOSE_TIMEOUT", 30.0)),
                  retries=3)

    @agent.output_validator
    def _valid(out: MaterialChoice) -> MaterialChoice:
        problem = check_choice(req, research, materials, out.material_number.strip() or None)
        if problem:
            if trace:
                trace.event("choose", "choice_refused", requirement=req.requirement_id, chose=out.material_number,
                            problem=problem)
            raise ModelRetry(problem)
        return out

    listing = "\n".join(_describe(n, r, research) for n, r in materials.items())
    prompt = f"Requirement {req.requirement_id}: {_want(req)}.\nInspected ERP materials:\n{listing}"
    started = time.monotonic()
    try:
        choice = (await agent.run(prompt)).output
    except Exception as error:
        return None, [f"{req.requirement_id}: no valid choice ({type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:120]})"]
    if trace:
        trace.event("choose", "material", requirement=req.requirement_id, chose=choice.material_number,
                    why=choice.why, seconds=round(time.monotonic() - started, 1))
    return choice.material_number.strip() or None, []

        async with self.lock:

async def paginate(session: SiteSession, list_ref: str | None = None, next_ref: str | None = None,
                   max_pages: int = MAX_PAGES) -> Listing:
    """Page through one list: read its rows, click its next / load-more control, read again, until no new row shows
    (past the end, sites repeat the last page or show nothing new). Every page goes through `session.look()`, so the
    worker's grounding check has seen each row."""
    notes: list[str] = []
    await session.look()  # refs for the current page
    first = await _rows(session, list_ref, None)
    if not first["rows"]:
        return Listing([], 1, first.get("how") or "no list found", ["no list with repeated rows found here"])
    path, how = first["path"], first["how"]
    seen: dict[str, Row] = {}
    for row in first["rows"]:
        seen.setdefault(_signature(row), Row(row["text"], row["links"]))
    pages = 1
    capped = False
    control_name = None
    while pages < max_pages and len(seen) < MAX_ROWS:
        if next_ref and pages == 1:
            ref = next_ref
        else:
            controls = await _next_controls(session, path)
            if control_name:
                controls = [c for c in controls if c["name"] == control_name] or controls[:1]
            if not controls:
                break
            ref = controls[0]["ref"]
            control_name = controls[0]["name"]
        before = len(seen)
        view = await session.act("click", ref, _click)
        if view.startswith("No element") or view.startswith("click "):
            notes.append(f"could not follow the list's control {ref}: {view.splitlines()[0][:120]}")
            break
        pages += 1
        current = await _rows(session, None, path)
        if not current["rows"]:
            current = await _rows(session, None, None)
        for row in seen.values():
            row.current = False
        for row in current["rows"]:
            key = _signature(row)
            if key in seen:
                seen[key].current, seen[key].links = True, row["links"]
            else:
                seen[key] = Row(row["text"], row["links"])
        if len(seen) == before:  # nothing new: the end of the list (past it, sites repeat the last page)
            break
    else:
        capped = True
        notes.append(f"stopped after {pages} pages / {len(seen)} rows; the list may go on")
    if pages > 1:  # the model never saw the pages clicked through: its next view comes whole, not as a diff
        session.shown = session.base = ()
    session.trace.event(session.name, "paginate", how=how, pages=pages, rows=len(seen), capped=capped)
    return Listing(list(seen.values()), pages, how, notes, capped)


def _format(listing: Listing, header: str) -> str:
    lines = [header]
    for i, row in enumerate(listing.rows[:MAX_ROWS], 1):
        text = row.text[:ROW_CHARS] + ("…" if len(row.text) > ROW_CHARS else "")
        links = []
        for link in row.links:
            name = (link["text"] or "")[:40]
            target = f' -> {link["href"]}' if link["href"] else ""
            ref = f'{link["ref"]} ' if link["ref"] and row.current else ""
            if name or target:
                links.append(f'[{ref}"{name}"{target}]')
        lines.append(f"{i}. {text}" + (f"  links: {' '.join(links)}" if links else ""))
    if not listing.rows:
        lines.append("(no rows)")
    for note in listing.notes:
        lines.append(f"Note: {note}")
    if any(not r.current for r in listing.rows):
        lines.append("Rows without refs are on earlier pages: open them with goto(their link target), or page back.")
    if any(r.current and r.links for r in listing.rows):
        lines.append("Refs in this list hold until your next action; this list stays with you, refs do not.")
    return "\n".join(lines)

# Building your agent

Your agent system has to be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the information and makes
the decisions, at run time. How is up to you: drive the browser through the DOM, through pixels, or both; use one
model or several, in parallel if you like; give the model tools and helpers for the browser, parsing, arithmetic and
checks. The model chooses where to go, what to search for and which documents matter. Rejected in review: a fixed
script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback, and a crawler that collects the
websites and hands everything to the model at the end.

## The browser

In the sandbox a headful Chromium runs on the desktop (`DISPLAY=:1`, 1280×800) with CDP on
`127.0.0.1:9222`.

- **DOM agents:** attach with Playwright (`chromium.connect_over_cdp(CDP_URL)`) or any CDP client.
- **Pixel agents:** take screenshots and send mouse and keyboard input to the desktop (`xdotool` and
  ImageMagick's `import` are installed), for example to drive Claude's computer-use tool.
- **Locally:** without `CDP_URL`, launch your own Chromium. The websites are the same: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"`
  gives your agent the scouting logins in `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, the way a run gets its logins.

### Several browsers

To work on several websites at once, ask for up to four browsers in `agent.json`:

```json
{"setup": ["npm", "ci"], "run": ["node", "agent.js"], "browsers": 2}
```

Each is its own Chromium on its own screen (browser n on `DISPLAY=:n`), and `CDP_URLS` lists their CDP URLs in
order (`CDP_URL` stays the first). With Playwright:

```javascript
import { chromium } from "playwright"

const sites = JSON.parse(process.env.CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS)
const browsers = await Promise.all(JSON.parse(process.env.CDP_URLS).map((url) => chromium.connectOverCDP(url)))
const pages = browsers.map((browser) => browser.contexts()[0].pages()[0])
await Promise.all([pages[0].goto(sites[0].url), pages[1].goto(sites[1].url)])
```

At most 4 browsers run at a time. Use tabs (`context.newPage()`) and browser contexts (`browser.newContext()`)
inside them as freely as you like, but don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included: the sandbox stops
them and says so in the run's logs. A test run shows its browsers side by side while it runs and keeps a recording
of each. Locally there is no `CDP_URLS`: on your machine your agent starts its own browsers.

## Models

The hosted models are free to use. Every run gets `QWEN_BASE_URL` and `QWEN_API_KEY` for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, an
OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls and images; on your machine `atira scout --env` sets the same variables,
pointed at `atira models proxy`. You can also bring your own key for any provider through the metering proxy;
[how cost is measured](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#how-cost-is-measured) has the details. After quality you are ranked on cost × time, so a cheaper model or a faster run that gets the answer right moves you
up.

## What makes it hard, on purpose

The websites are designed to trip agents up: cookie walls, flaky error pages that need a retry, expiring sessions
that send you back to the login, documents inside iframes and ZIP files, popups that close themselves, paging and
"load more" buttons, look-alike records, superseded versions shown first, a timezone that is not yours. Treat
every page as adversarial and verify what you read.

## Tips

- Read the brief's rules carefully: they define the one correct answer.
- Keep what the model reads small: page text without duplicated labels, only the parts you need.
- Use prompt caching for your system prompt and tool definitions.
- Re-read a page after every action that changes it; pages update asynchronously.
- Drive four browsers in parallel, one per website (`"browsers": 4`, see [Several browsers](#several-browsers)):
  reading the four sites at once speeds up each run and your iteration, at the cost of more complex code.
- Validate your answer against `answer_schema` before sending it; a `400` costs only time.
- Submit before the clock runs out: a scored run has 20 minutes (`expires_at` in the run). Every part of the answer
  scores on its own, so have your agent submit its best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
  searching; a run that ends without an answer scores 0.
- Develop against the public websites locally (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox (`atira test-run`):
  a test run shows the full score breakdown, so use it to find what your agent gets wrong.
- Work the answer out from the websites: the final run, which weighs most for the winners, uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it.

## Starter kit

[`starter-kit/`](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz) is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and
submits an answer, attaches to the run's browsers over CDP with Playwright, and shows one call to each hosted model.
Your agent goes in `solve()` in `agent.py`; out of the box it exits without an answer. Start from it or from scratch.

# Fair play

**Rules at a glance**

You submit an agentic system: one agent or several. In the sandbox it does the whole job on its own: finds what it needs on the four websites, works out the bid and submits it. Nobody helps it during a run.

**Not allowed**

- **Hardcoding:** copying values from the websites into your package (prices, material numbers, totals, discounts, logins, TANs), including in prompts and notes, also as defaults or fallbacks. Using what the task brief tells every team, like the sales director's mailbox, is fine.
- **Pre-solving:** working out the answer yourself, or having an AI assistant do it, and putting the result in your package. Exploring the sites with an assistant is fine.
- **Scripts instead of agents:** a fixed click path, or a crawler that grabs everything for one model call. A model has to choose where to go, what to search for and what matters.
- **Outside help during a run:** contacting anything besides our platform and the four websites, calling a model other than through our proxy (your own API keys work through it), running a model inside the sandbox, or starting your own browsers (use the up to 4 provided). Setup may install dependencies.

**How it's checked:** an AI reviewer reads every submitted package before its scored run. Unclear cases are flagged and stay off the leaderboard until an organizer has looked. The final runs on websites and data your system hasn't seen.

The details follow.

## Allowed

- Any agent design; the free hosted models, or any provider and model with your own key, through the proxy; any
  amount of tokens.
  The proxy forwards your calls unchanged and measures them: reported usage is metered at the published model
  prices, and an upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. See [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls)
  for SDK configuration.
- Keeping your model key as a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets) rather than in your package.
- Your own code, prompts and tools; open-source libraries installed during setup.
- Using what you learned with the scouting logins and in test runs about how the websites work.
- Up to 4 browsers at a time: ask for them with `"browsers"` in `agent.json` and use as many tabs and browser
  contexts inside them as you like.

## Not allowed

- Hardcoding values copied from the public scenario or its websites into code, config, prompts or notes, including defaults and fallbacks: tender references, material numbers, prices, totals, discounts, logins and TANs. Facts the task brief states for every scenario, such as the sales director's mailbox, are
  rules you may use.
- A scripted solution. Your agent system must be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the
  information and makes the decisions. Code can help it (browser control, parsing, arithmetic, checks, reading a
  page or document the model chose, paging through results it asked for), and several agents and browsers may work
  in parallel. Rejected: a fixed script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback,
  and a crawler that collects the websites and hands everything to the model at the end.
- Bundling or running a local model, or reaching any model other than through the proxy.
- Contacting hosts other than the API and the challenge's websites, or trying to get data out of the sandbox.
- Starting browsers of your own in the sandbox, headless ones included. At most 4 browsers run at a time: ask for up
  to 4 in `agent.json` (`"browsers"`), use tabs and browser contexts inside them freely, and don't start others.
  On your own machine (developing with the scouting logins) your agent starts its own browsers; that is up to you.
- Attacking the platform, the websites, the sandbox or other teams; sharing scored-run data.

## How it is checked

- **Package review before any scored run:** an AI code reviewer, a coding agent that reads your whole package in an
  isolated VM. Outcomes: passed, flagged or rejected (no runs). A flagged package still runs and scores, but its

Your agent system has to be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the information and makes

websites and hands everything to the model at the end.

## The browser

In the sandbox a headful Chromium runs on the desktop (`DISPLAY=:1`, 1280×800) with CDP on
`127.0.0.1:9222`.

- **DOM agents:** attach with Playwright (`chromium.connect_over_cdp(CDP_URL)`) or any CDP client.
- **Pixel agents:** take screenshots and send mouse and keyboard input to the desktop (`xdotool` and
  ImageMagick's `import` are installed), for example to drive Claude's computer-use tool.
- **Locally:** without `CDP_URL`, launch your own Chromium. The websites are the same: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"`
  gives your agent the scouting logins in `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, the way a run gets its logins.

### Several browsers

To work on several websites at once, ask for up to four browsers in `agent.json`:

```json
{"setup": ["npm", "ci"], "run": ["node", "agent.js"], "browsers": 2}
```

Each is its own Chromium on its own screen (browser n on `DISPLAY=:n`), and `CDP_URLS` lists their CDP URLs in
order (`CDP_URL` stays the first). With Playwright:

```javascript
import { chromium } from "playwright"

const sites = JSON.parse(process.env.CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS)
const browsers = await Promise.all(JSON.parse(process.env.CDP_URLS).map((url) => chromium.connectOverCDP(url)))
const pages = browsers.map((browser) => browser.contexts()[0].pages()[0])
await Promise.all([pages[0].goto(sites[0].url), pages[1].goto(sites[1].url)])
```

At most 4 browsers run at a time. Use tabs (`context.newPage()`) and browser contexts (`browser.newContext()`)
inside them as freely as you like, but don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included: the sandbox stops
them and says so in the run's logs. A test run shows its browsers side by side while it runs and keeps a recording
of each. Locally there is no `CDP_URLS`: on your machine your agent starts its own browsers.

## Models

The hosted models are free to use. Every run gets `QWEN_BASE_URL` and `QWEN_API_KEY` for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, an
OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls and images; on your machine `atira scout --env` sets the same variables,

up.

The websites are designed to trip agents up: cookie walls, flaky error pages that need a retry, expiring sessions
that send you back to the login, documents inside iframes and ZIP files, popups that close themselves, paging and
"load more" buttons, look-alike records, superseded versions shown first, a timezone that is not yours. Treat
every page as adversarial and verify what you read.

- Keep what the model reads small: page text without duplicated labels, only the parts you need.

content.text: The strongest unexplored option is to reuse mail discoveries within the same run. Today nine record kinds each search inbox and archive independently, even when their result lists overlap. A shared index of results from model-chosen searches could remove repeated browsing while keeping the model responsible for selecting and validating records.

The strongest unexplored option is to reuse mail discoveries within the same run. Today nine record kinds each search inbox and archive independently, even when their result lists overlap. A shared index of results from model-chosen searches could remove repeated browsing while keeping the model responsible for selecting and validating records.

The best novel experiment is a **shared, in-run mailbox index**. Qwen would still choose searches and records, but later workers could reuse results already discovered by another worker. Today nine mail kinds independently search folders; mail accounted for 64–92 worker requests in two successful runs. First measure overlap in result links, then test reuse with a fresh-search fallback. The pitch: **“Discover evidence once; let the agent decide how to use it.”**

Next, verify completed facts while mail research continues, then check only new or replaced facts at the end. This targets the observed 29–58 seconds spent verifying after the last mail result, though repeated verifier prompts could raise tokens.

I would defer selective skipping of mail kinds until we can prove from completed tender and ERP facts that a kind has no downstream use. Clef is promising only as a targeted dead-end detector; the local evaluation does not support using it for record selection or summarization. A separate summarizer adds latency and risks losing exact references, dates, or senders.

These designs fit the challenge’s [fair-play rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md): the model directs searches and selects evidence; helpers may retain and process results it chose.

    (navigation, thinking off), a model decides the current revision (thinking on), the worker opens it and pages
    through it, and a model extracts each page (thinking on, in parallel).

    if choice is None:

    want = " ".join(option.split())

    return None


def _close_options(texts: list[str], option: str, limit: int = 8) -> list[str]:

    want = option.casefold().strip()
    hits = [t for t in texts if want and want in t.casefold()]
    if not hits:
        words = [w for w in want.replace(",", " ").split() if len(w) > 1]
        hits = [t for t in texts if any(w in t.casefold() for w in words)]
    return hits[:limit]

VALUE_RUN = re.compile(r"[\w/.:,+-]+")
DIGIT = re.compile(r"\d")


def unseen_values(text: str, seen: str) -> list[str]:
    """The values in `text` (anything with a digit: numbers, references, dates) that `seen` does not contain."""
    missing = []  # a value holds no whitespace, so searching `seen` as is matches its whitespace-normalised form
    for token in VALUE_RUN.findall(text):
        if not DIGIT.search(token):
            continue
        token = token.strip(".,:;/-+")
        if token and token not in seen and token not in missing:
            missing.append(token)
    return missing

    """Record a fact you can see on the current page (copy values exactly), so it survives if you run out of time."""

    if missing:

    ctx.deps.notes[key] = value

def _norm(text: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(text.replace("​", "").split()).casefold()


def ground(extraction: Extraction, view: str) -> tuple[dict[str, dict], list[str]]:
    """Keep the fields whose quote (or, failing that, whose value) appears in the view; the rest are dropped."""
    haystack = _norm(_strip_refs(view))
    kept: dict[str, dict] = {}
    dropped: list[str] = []
    for found in extraction.fields:
        value, quote = found.value.strip(), found.quote.strip()
        if not value:
            dropped.append(f"{found.name} (not shown)")
            continue
        if quote and _norm(quote) in haystack:
            kept[found.name] = {"value": value, "quote": quote}
        elif len(_norm(value)) >= 2 and _norm(value) in haystack:
            kept[found.name] = {"value": value, "quote": value, "note": "quote was not verbatim; the value is on "
                                                                           "the page"}
        else:
            dropped.append(f"{found.name} (its quote is not on the page)")
    return kept, dropped


def readings(value: str) -> str:
    """Deterministic readings of a value for the model: number with locale, both dates when the order is open."""
    out = []
    if not re.search(r"\d", value):
        return ""
    try:
        when = read_date(value)
        if when.readings:
            tag = "" if not when.ambiguous else " (day/month order ambiguous)"
            out.append("date: " + " or ".join(r.isoformat() for r in when.readings) + tag)
        elif when.partial:
            out.append("month/day: " + " or ".join(f"{m:02d}-{d:02d}" for m, d in when.partial)
                       + (" (order ambiguous)" if when.ambiguous else ""))
        return "; ".join(out)  # a date is not also a number
    except ParseError:
        pass
    try:
        number = read_number(value)
        if number.ambiguous:
            out.append("number: " + " or ".join(str(r) for r in number.readings) + " (separator ambiguous)")
        elif re.search(r"[.,]", value):
            out.append(f"number: {number.value}" + (f" ({number.locale})" if number.locale else ""))
    except ParseError:
        pass
    return "; ".join(out)


async def extract_fields(session: SiteSession, fields: dict[str, str], *, thinking: bool = False) -> str:
    view = _strip_refs(session.view)[:VIEW_CHARS]
    agent = Agent(llm.model(), output_type=Extraction, instructions=EXTRACT_INSTRUCTIONS,
                  model_settings=llm.settings(thinking), retries=2)
    asked = "\n".join(f"- {name}: {description}" for name, description in fields.items())
    prompt = f"Fields:\n{asked}\n\nPage text:\n{view}"
    try:
        result = await agent.run(prompt)
    except Exception as error:  # a refused or hung call: the worker goes on reading the view itself
        session.trace.event(session.name, "extract_failed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:160]}")
        return "extract failed this time; read the values off the current view instead."
    kept, dropped = ground(result.output, view)
    usage = result.usage
    session.trace.event(session.name, "extract", fields=list(fields), kept=list(kept), dropped=dropped,
                        input_tokens=usage.input_tokens, output_tokens=usage.output_tokens)
    lines = [f"Extracted from the current view ({session.page.url}):"]
    for name in fields:
        if name in kept:
            hit = kept[name]
            line = f"- {name}: {hit['value']}  (quote: \"{hit['quote'][:200]}\")"
            parsed = readings(hit["value"])
            if parsed:
                line += f"  [{parsed}]"
            if "note" in hit:
                line += f"  ({hit['note']})"
            lines.append(line)
    if dropped:
        lines.append("Not extracted: " + "; ".join(dropped) + ". Open the view that shows them if you need them.")
    out = "\n".join(lines)
    session.seen += "\n" + out  # the readings are derived from page values, so the grounding check accepts them
    return out


async def extract(ctx: RunContext[Deps], fields: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    """Read several facts off the current view in one step: give {field name: what it is} and each field comes back
    with its value exactly as the page writes it, the quote it comes from and, for numbers and dates, how it reads
    (locale, or both readings when the day/month order is open). Fields the page does not show are listed as not
    extracted; nothing is guessed. Use it after opening the record or view that holds the facts."""
    return await extract_fields(ctx.deps.session, fields)

- Only MM03, MMBE, VK13 exist; direct URLs work (`/mm03`, `/mmbe`, `/vk13?material=X`).
- Search popup `/search?transaction=..&q=..`; search the Kataloggruppe. Result rows already list most attributes,

- MM03: technical tab (certification in tooltip); planning tab (status in tooltip, hidden decoy "01"; lead time
  from stock and production lead time).
- MMBE: the summary includes blocked stock (trap); use the free stock line.
- VK13: one condition record per page, older years later; validity, currency + FX key, price unit (1 or 100 ST);
  scales under `view=scales`, listed descending.
- No ordinary setup fee in the ERP; it comes from the tender Q&A.

## Architecture

```
agent/
  agent.py         orchestrator: reads run, shared findings store, starts workers, deadline (submit by T-90 s)
  llm.py           Qwen client, retry/backoff, thinking flag, usage log, stable prompts for caching
  browser_tools.py model-invoked tools (below) plus automatic overlay/gate/session handling
  extract.py       cleaned page text: visible only, details expanded, aria-labels, tooltips, iframes, no U+200B
  worker.py        generic loop: role prompt + goal + tools, step budget, deadline
  roles.py         generic role prompts: tender, spec, erp, mail
  evidence.py      pydantic records for each fact type
  calc.py          deterministic bid rules: rounding, scales, FX, packaging, setup pool, bonus (unit-tested)
  submit.py        configurator fill + TAN signing
```

Tools: `goto`, `click(ref)`, `fill(ref, text)`, `select(ref, value)`, `read_page`, `read_frame`, `next_page`,
`search(q)`, `screenshot` (fallback), `finish(result)`. Automatic: login with run credentials, consent, closing
decoy modals via x, unlocking gates, retrying flaky pages, re-login on expiry.

Fair-play line: the model chooses where to go, what to search, which revision / record / mail applies. Helpers only
extract a chosen page, paginate a chosen result set, calculate and fill forms.

## Scoring (what each version buys)

Per bid: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, total 5, arithmetic consistency 5, withdrawn-Q&A check 5,
metal-index check 5, positions the rest (65 with both extra checks). Within each position: material 20 %,
quantity 15 %, base price 15 %, surcharge 10 %, packaging 10 %, bonus 10 %, final unit price 10 %, delivery 10 %.
Every field scores on its own, so each version adds fields and always ends with a signed bid.

## Roadmap

Each version is done when a sandbox test run (`atira test-run .`) shows the listed fields correct in the score
breakdown and finishes well under 20 minutes. Submit (`atira submit .`) after each version that beats our best.

### v0: harness (half a day)

- `llm.py`: pydantic-ai model for Qwen, thinking on/off settings, retries, usage logging.
- `extract.py`: cleaned page text (visible only, details expanded, aria-labels, tooltips, iframes, no U+200B).
- `browser_tools.py`: goto, click, fill, select, read_page, next_page, finish; automatic consent, decoy-modal
  close, gate unlock, flaky-page retry, re-login on expiry.
- `worker.py`: one pydantic-ai Agent per role, deps = page + findings store, step budget, deadline.
- Trace log per run (steps, tool calls, tokens, seconds) to see where time goes.
- Done when: a worker logs into each of the four scouting sites and reads one chosen page correctly.

**v0 status (2026-10-10): built.** `extract.py`, `browser_tools.py`, `worker.py`, `llm.py`, `tracing.py`;
check with `dev/smoke.py`. Learnings:

- Hosted Qwen sometimes hangs a call for ~300 s; the client times out after 30 s and retries (`LLM_TIMEOUT`).
  Steps then take 1 to 4 s.
- Gates re-lock on every mail page, so the generic "slide to unlock / not a robot" helper saves 4 to 6 steps
  per page. The ERP receipt-number gate is still solved by the model (works).
- Qwen invents values from memory once old views are trimmed. `note()` and worker results are checked: every
  value with a digit must appear on a page that worker saw, otherwise it goes back to the model. Thinking on
  invents less on document-heavy sites (tender, spec) at ~3 s per step.
- Smoke result: ERP 14 s and mail 18 s, correct and grounded; tender and spec read the right pages and note
  correct facts but hit the 25-step limit on broad goals. v1 goals must be narrow, with thinking on there.
- Open: a model that repeats a refused note loops; escalate after two refusals.

### v1: eligible signed bid (~10 to 15 points)

- Tender worker: reference, positions with units, bidder data from the brief.
- Configurator: Hauptangebot, omit every position, discount 0, total 0, decline AGB, request TAN.
- Mail worker: newest TAN, then sign and accept the confirm, all within the TAN's 5 minutes.
- Done when: reference and decision correct, the run is eligible.

### v2: materials, quantities, delivery (~+30)

- Tender worker reads the Q&A: quantity changes, withdrawals (withdrawn-Q&A check), Satz positions.
- Spec worker: current revision, requirement per position, Kataloggruppe, pieces per Satz.
- ERP worker: Kataloggruppe search, exact attribute match, active status; stock and both lead times.
- `calc.py`: final quantities, shared-stock rule, lead time; no_bid when a material is missing.
- Configurator fills material, quantity, lead time; price fields still blank or omitted per field.
- Done when: material, quantity, delivery correct per position.

### v3: prices, discount, totals (~+25)

- ERP worker: condition record valid on the scenario date, scales, price unit, currency + FX key.
- Mail worker: director approvals (exact reference, latest, conditional threshold), Devisenfixing.
- `calc.py`: base price with FX, discount clauses default rule, final unit price, total, HALF_UP everywhere.
- Done when: base price, discount, final unit price, total and arithmetic consistency correct.

### v4: clause rules (remaining points)

- Konditionsgruppen + Konditionsregeln (discount scope per position).
- Scoped amendments + Technikfreigabe (nutzbarer Weg) before material matching.
- Metal index (validity window) for the mass surcharge; packaging tariffs and cartons; Terminfreigabe
  commitments; Ruestpools shared setup with cent allocation; Projektbonus bands with largest-remainder split.
- Done when: every field in the breakdown is correct on public-1.

### v5: speed, cost, generalisation

- Four browsers, one per site, workers start as soon as their inputs are known.
- Thinking only on decision steps, trimmed snapshots, stable prompts for cache hits.
- Hard deadline guard: sign whatever is ready by T-90 s.

"""
The agent's entry point: agent.json runs `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`, in the sandbox and on your machine.

v2: read the brief, then the orchestrator (planner, findings board, research workers, verifier, calc) builds the
answer, and submit.py enters and signs the bid with it; without an answer every position is omitted, as in v1.
AGENT_RESEARCH=0 skips the research (the v1 path). See docs/plan.md.
"""
import asyncio
import json
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import localenv  # noqa: F401  (first: local runs read agent/.env before any module reads its settings)
import browser_tools
import browsers
import loopwatch
import run as contract
from briefing import read_brief
from browser_tools import SiteSession
from orchestrator import Orchestrator
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
from submit import BidFlow, Mailbox, submit_bid
import tracing
from tracing import Trace

SAFETY_SECONDS = 90  # the answer must be in before the run expires
LOCAL_SECONDS = 20 * 60  # the scouting run does not expire; behave like a scored run
RESEARCH_START_SECONDS = 600  # a website that only research needs is warmed this long, then given up


def warm_up(sessions: dict[str, SiteSession], deadline: float, critical: set[str]) -> dict[str, asyncio.Task]:
    """
    Start signing in to every website in the background and return at once: nothing waits for all of them. The
    `critical` ones (the bid website, the mailbox) keep retrying until START_MARGIN before the deadline; the others
    give up after RESEARCH_START_SECONDS. A session whose start is still running can be handed out: its first look
    waits for the start (SiteSession.revive).
    """
    browser_tools.DEADLINE = deadline
    tasks = {}
    for name, session in sessions.items():
        limit = deadline - browser_tools.START_MARGIN
        if name not in critical:
            limit = min(limit, time.monotonic() + RESEARCH_START_SECONDS)
        session.until = limit
        tasks[name] = asyncio.create_task(session.start(until=limit), name=f"start@{name}")
        tasks[name].add_done_callback(lambda t: t.cancelled() or t.exception())  # failures are traced in start
    return tasks


async def solve(task: dict, page, answer: dict | None = None,
                attributes: dict[str, dict[str, str]] | None = None) -> dict | None:
    """
    Enter the bid on the run's website (a "site" submission) and return None.

    `answer` (calc's BidResult.answer()) and `attributes` (per position, the chosen material's attributes) are what
    the bid worker enters; positions they do not give completely are omitted. Unless given, the orchestrator
    researches them; a research failure never costs the signed bid.
    """
    trace = Trace()
    loopwatch.Watchdog(activity=lambda: trace.last).start()  # a blocked loop or a silent run dumps its stacks
    left = min(contract.seconds_left(task), LOCAL_SECONDS)
    deadline = time.monotonic() + left - SAFETY_SECONDS
    # Sign in to every website in the background: the brief, the planner and the workers never wait for all of
    # them. The bid website (named by the run contract) keeps warming; the mailbox too, once the brief names it.
    contexts = await browsers.more_contexts(page, len(task["access"]))
    sessions = {site["siteId"]: SiteSession(site, context, trace) for site, context in zip(task["access"], contexts)}
    contract_site = (task.get("submission") or {}).get("siteId")
    starts = warm_up(sessions, deadline, {contract_site} if contract_site in sessions else set(sessions))
    briefing = await read_brief(task)
    # The run contract names the submission website; it wins over the model's reading of the brief.
    if contract_site in sessions and contract_site != briefing.bid_site:
        trace.event("briefing", "bid_site_corrected", read=briefing.bid_site, contract=contract_site)
        briefing = briefing.model_copy(update={"bid_site": contract_site})
    trace.event("briefing", "done", **briefing.model_dump(exclude={"submission_steps"}))
    bid, mail = sessions[briefing.bid_site], sessions[briefing.mail_site]
    for session in (bid, mail):  # critical after all: warm until the margin before the deadline
        session.until = max(session.until or 0, deadline - browser_tools.START_MARGIN)
    # The bid form's steps that need no research (bidder data, offer type) run while the research does.
    flow = BidFlow(bid, Mailbox(mail, briefing, deadline), briefing, deadline)
    flow.start()
    if answer is None and os.environ.get("AGENT_RESEARCH", "1") != "0":
        answer, attributes = await research(task, briefing, contexts, trace, deadline, sessions)
    # A start still running is waited for by the session's first look; one that gave up gets a fresh tab there.
    trace.event("starts", "state", **{name: ("up" if s.ok else "starting" if s.starting else "down")
                                      for name, s in sessions.items()}, pending=sum(not t.done() for t in starts.values()))
    try:
        result = await flow.finish(answer, attributes)
    except Exception as error:  # never end without trying to sign: one more pass with what is on screen
        trace.event("submit", "crashed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:300]}")
        result = await submit_bid(bid, Mailbox(mail, briefing, deadline), briefing, deadline, answer, attributes)
    trace.event("result", "done", result=result.model_dump() if result else None)
    return None


async def research(task: dict, briefing, contexts: list, trace: Trace, deadline: float,
                   warm: dict[str, SiteSession] | None = None) -> tuple[dict | None, dict[str, dict[str, str]] | None]:
    """The orchestrator's answer and material attributes; (None, None) when it fails or builds nothing."""
    answer, attributes, problems = None, None, []
    orchestrator = None
    started = time.monotonic()
    try:
        orchestrator = Orchestrator(task, briefing, {s["siteId"]: c for s, c in zip(task["access"], contexts)},
                                    trace, deadline, warm=warm)
        problems = orchestrator.board.problems
        answer, _ = await orchestrator.run()
        attributes = orchestrator.attributes
    except Exception as error:  # the signed bid must never be lost to a research failure
        trace.event("orchestrator", "failed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:300]}")
    if answer is None and orchestrator is not None:  # still the reference, decision and any discount read
        answer = orchestrator.fallback_answer()
    trace.event("orchestrator", "done", seconds=round(time.monotonic() - started, 1), answer=answer,
                attributes=attributes, problems=problems[:30])
    path = Path(trace.path).with_name("answer.json")
    path.write_text(json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
    print(f"Answer for the bid form written to {path}", flush=True)
    return answer, attributes


async def main() -> int:
    task, token = contract.load_run()
    sites = ", ".join(f"{site.get('siteId')} {site.get('url')}" for site in task["access"])
    print(f"Run {task.get('run_id') or '(local: the scouting logins, nothing counts)'}; websites: {sites}; "
          f"answer via {task['submission']['kind']}", flush=True)
    async with async_playwright() as playwright:
        browser, page = await browsers.connect(playwright)  # more browsers: browsers.connect(playwright, 1), ...
        try:
            answer = await solve(task, page)
        finally:  # the platform keeps only the last lines of a run's output: repeat the phases there

A bounded, read-only query tool for a **model-selected page** is feasible and allowed by the [fair-play rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md). It could return selected rows and fields with source quotes and element references, avoiding an extra model extraction call on dense pages. Use the agent’s existing visible-DOM walker as its input; raw HTML would include hidden decoys and miss some frame content.

The smallest test is one dense ERP or Q&A page: compare the current tools with a scoped query for accuracy, model calls, tokens, and elapsed time. Arbitrary Python or page JavaScript execution would grant far more access than page analysis needs.

Most of the pasted proposal is already implemented: four-browser parallel research, deterministic Decimal calculations, typed evidence, DOM extraction, prompt caching, and parallel record readers. Clef performed worse than Qwen on link and record choices in the local evaluation. A 2–3 minute run is an ambition, not an estimate supported by current measurements.

"""
run_code tool — execute arbitrary Python in the persistent sandboxed kernel.
"""

import logging

import logfire
from pydantic_ai import RunContext

from .....deps import HancasDeps
from .....exceptions import KernelNotAvailableError
from ...registry import hancas_tool
from .config import (
    get_run_code_default_timeout,
    get_run_code_max_output_chars,
    get_run_code_max_timeout,
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@hancas_tool(requires_kernel=True, sequential=True)
async def run_code(
    ctx: RunContext[HancasDeps],
    code: str,
    timeout_seconds: int | None = None,
) -> str:
    """
    Execute Python code in a persistent sandboxed kernel and return stdout/stderr.

    The kernel is a clean Python process — state (variables, imports) persists
    across calls within one patient run.  Do not call this tool multiple times
    in parallel; always call it sequentially so each call can build on the state
    left by the previous one.

    Errors and tracebacks are returned as plain text so you can read them,
    fix the code, and call again.

    :param ctx: Tool run context with kernel_executor in deps.
    :param code: Valid Python source code to execute.
    :param timeout_seconds: Wall-clock seconds to wait for this cell to complete.
    :return: Combined stdout, expression results, and tracebacks as plain text.
    """
    executor = ctx.deps.kernel_executor
    if executor is None:
        raise KernelNotAvailableError(
            "kernel_executor is None: requires_kernel=True should have caused "
            + "_run_with_kernel to inject an executor before this tool was called. "
            + "This is a system misconfiguration — aborting."
        )

    default_timeout = get_run_code_default_timeout()
    max_timeout = get_run_code_max_timeout()
    effective_timeout = min(
        timeout_seconds if timeout_seconds is not None else default_timeout,
        max_timeout,
    )

    with logfire.span(
        "kernel_execute",
        code_length=len(code),
        code=code,
        timeout_seconds=effective_timeout,
    ) as span:
        output = await executor.execute(code, timeout=float(effective_timeout))
        timed_out = "[Execution timed out]" in output
        has_error = timed_out or "Error (" in output
        span.set_attribute("output_length", len(output))
        span.set_attribute("has_error", has_error)
        span.set_attribute("timed_out", timed_out)
        if output:
            span.set_attribute("output", output[:8192])
        if has_error:
            span.set_level("error")

        if timed_out:
            if effective_timeout < max_timeout:
                output = output.replace(
                    "[Execution timed out]",
                    f"[Execution timed out after {effective_timeout}s, retry with a higher timeout_seconds value (max: {max_timeout}s), split it across multiple cells, or try a simpler approach]",
                )
            else:
                output = output.replace(
                    "[Execution timed out]",
                    f"[Execution timed out after {effective_timeout}s, already at the maximum allowed timeout ({max_timeout}s). Split it across multiple cells or try a simpler approach]",
                )

        # Capped last so the timeout hint survives in the retained tail. Only the
        # tool path is capped: sweeps machine-parse predict() output through
        # KernelExecutor.execute and must stay whole.
        return _truncate_output(output, get_run_code_max_output_chars())


def _truncate_output(output: str, max_chars: int) -> str:
    """
    Bound a single cell's output before it enters the model's context.

    Drops the middle rather than the end: the head carries what the cell set out
    to show, and the tail carries the exception line and the timeout hint.

    :param output: Raw cell output.
    :param max_chars: Ceiling on the returned string's payload, split two thirds
        head and one third tail. The marker itself is added on top of it.
    :return: ``output`` unchanged when within the ceiling, else head + marker + tail.
    """
    if len(output) <= max_chars:
        return output
    head_chars = (max_chars * 2) // 3
    tail_chars = max_chars - head_chars
    dropped = len(output) - max_chars
    marker = (
        f"\n\n[... {dropped:,} of {len(output):,} characters omitted: output exceeded the "
        f"{max_chars:,}-character limit. Head and tail are shown. Re-running will not show "
        f"more; print a summary or a subset instead ...]\n\n"
    )
    return output[:head_chars] + marker + output[-tail_chars:]
"""Per-kernel bubblewrap launch-command construction.

``_build_kernel_cmd`` assembles the ``apptainer exec instance://<name> bwrap
<recipe> python -m ipykernel`` argv that builds the inner per-kernel sandbox from
the persistent instance's host passthrough (started by the ``sandbox_runtime``
module). Pure argv construction: no process is started here.
"""

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Final

# Consumed by other modules in this package: ``_build_kernel_cmd`` by the
# ``kernel`` module, ``_uv_python_info`` by ``sandbox_runtime``.
__all__ = ["_THREAD_LIMIT_ENV_VARS", "_build_kernel_cmd", "_uv_python_info"]

# OpenMP / BLAS thread-limit env vars.  Set together so every threaded backend a
# kernel might touch honors the same per-kernel cap: XGBoost's OpenMP,
# numpy/scipy/sklearn via OpenBLAS or MKL, numexpr, and Accelerate/vecLib.  With
# the sweep pool running many kernels at once, leaving these unset lets each
# kernel spawn one thread per core, oversubscribing the CPU and wedging cells.
_THREAD_LIMIT_ENV_VARS: Final = (
    "OMP_NUM_THREADS",
    "OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS",
    "MKL_NUM_THREADS",
    "NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS",
    "VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS",
)

# Neutral in-sandbox mount points (bwrap remaps these two; every other path is
# bound at its real host path so preambles can reference it directly).
_SANDBOX_VENV: Final = Path("/sandbox/venv")
# uv-managed Python installations live outside /usr (e.g.
# ~/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-X.Y.Z-…/); mount at a neutral path.
_SANDBOX_CPYTHON: Final = Path("/uv_python")

# bwrap is shipped inside the SIF at /opt/bin (see hpc/hancas.def).  It cannot
# live in the container's /usr/bin because the instance bind-mounts the HOST /usr
# over it (needed for the GPU driver libs), which would shadow it; /opt is never
# bind-mounted, so this absolute path resolves to the in-image bwrap on every
# host — including NHR@FAU, where the host has no bwrap at all.
_BWRAP_BIN: Final = "/opt/bin/bwrap"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# uv-managed Python detection
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The venv's python is usually a symlink to a uv-managed CPython living outside
# /usr and sys.prefix (~/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-…).  bwrap cannot reach
# it via /usr, so it is mounted at the neutral path /uv_python and executed from
# there.  Returns (uv_python_mode, real_python_root).


def _uv_python_info() -> tuple[bool, Path]:
    real_python = Path(sys.executable).resolve()
    real_python_root = real_python.parent.parent  # …/cpython-X.Y.Z-…/ (bin/../)
    uv_mode = not (
        real_python_root.is_relative_to(Path("/usr"))
        or real_python_root.is_relative_to(Path(sys.prefix))
    )
    return uv_mode, real_python_root


def _lib_symlink_args() -> list[str]:
    """Recreate the host's /lib,/lib64,/bin,/sbin layout inside the fresh bwrap
    root.  On modern distros these are symlinks into /usr (resolved once /usr is
    bound); on older distros they are real dirs and are bound read-only.

    Without /lib64 the ELF interpreter (ld-linux-x86-64.so.2) is not found and
    execvp fails; without /bin, popen()/`/bin/sh` (used by XGBoost GPU init)
    fails with ENOENT.
    """
    args: list[str] = []
    for d in ("/lib", "/lib64", "/bin", "/sbin"):
        if os.path.islink(d):
            args += ["--symlink", os.readlink(d), d]
        elif os.path.isdir(d):
            args += ["--ro-bind", d, d]
    return args


def _build_kernel_cmd(
    *,
    instance_name: str | None,
    runtime_dir: Path | None,
    connection_file_name: str,
    dataset_path: Path | None = None,
    kb_models_path: Path | None = None,
    kb_models_readonly: bool = False,
    kb_functions_path: Path | None = None,
    kb_seeds_path: Path | None = None,
    prebuilt_db_path: Path | None = None,
    prebuilt_db_dir: Path | None = None,
    use_net_isolation: bool = False,
    thread_limit: int | None = None,
) -> list[str]:
    """Build the kernel launch argv for ``kernel_spec.argv``.

    When ``instance_name`` is None (HANCAS_NO_SANDBOX / macOS) returns a bare
    ``python -m ipykernel_launcher`` command.  Otherwise returns
    ``apptainer exec instance://<name> bwrap <recipe> python -m ipykernel …`` —
    the inner bwrap layer building the per-kernel sandbox.
    """
    _sandboxed = instance_name is not None
    uv_mode, real_python_root = _uv_python_info()

    if _sandboxed:
        if uv_mode:
            python_executable = str(
                _SANDBOX_CPYTHON / "bin" / Path(sys.executable).resolve().name
            )
        else:
            python_executable = str(_SANDBOX_VENV / "bin" / "python")
    else:
        python_executable = sys.executable

    launcher: list[str] = [
        python_executable,
        "-m",
        "ipykernel_launcher",
        "-f",
        str(runtime_dir / connection_file_name)
        if (_sandboxed and runtime_dir)
        else "{connection_file}",
    ]

    if not _sandboxed:
        return launcher

    assert runtime_dir is not None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Inner bwrap sandbox (built from the outer instance's host passthrough)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    bwrap: list[str] = [_BWRAP_BIN]

    # Venv and uv-managed Python remapped to neutral paths so sys.prefix does not
    # reveal the host project layout.
    bwrap += ["--ro-bind", sys.prefix, str(_SANDBOX_VENV)]
    if uv_mode:
        bwrap += ["--ro-bind", str(real_python_root), str(_SANDBOX_CPYTHON)]

    # System libraries: libpython, libzmq, libcuda, compiled extensions.
    bwrap += ["--ro-bind", "/usr", "/usr"]
    bwrap += _lib_symlink_args()
    bwrap += ["--ro-bind", "/etc", "/etc"]

    # /proc (CPython reads /proc/self/maps; ZMQ needs it) and /dev.
    bwrap += ["--proc", "/proc"]
    bwrap += ["--dev", "/dev"]

    # NVIDIA GPU device nodes — --dev-bind is required for character devices.
    for _nvidia_dev in sorted(Path("/dev").glob("nvidia*")):
        bwrap += ["--dev-bind", str(_nvidia_dev), str(_nvidia_dev)]

    # Private writable scratch — isolates /tmp per kernel (no cross-patient leak).
    bwrap += ["--tmpfs", "/tmp"]

    # Jupyter connection metadata, IPC sockets, and the network guard live here;
    # bound at the real host path so a single connection file works inside/out.
    bwrap += ["--bind", str(runtime_dir), str(runtime_dir)]

    # Dataset: read-only if requested; excluded otherwise so the kernel cannot
    # discover or exfiltrate the raw training data.
    if dataset_path is not None:
        bwrap += ["--ro-bind", str(dataset_path), str(dataset_path)]

    # Models directory: read-write so the agent can persist trained ML models; read-only for
    # sweep kernels, whose predict() must not leave files in the knowledge base.
    if kb_models_path is not None:
        kb_models_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        bind = "--ro-bind" if kb_models_readonly else "--bind"
        bwrap += [bind, str(kb_models_path), str(kb_models_path)]

    # Functions directory: read-only so the agent can hot-reload KB functions.
    if kb_functions_path is not None:
        kb_functions_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        bwrap += ["--ro-bind", str(kb_functions_path), str(kb_functions_path)]

    # Seeds directory: read-only so the synthesis agent can read all seed KBs.
    if kb_seeds_path is not None:
        bwrap += ["--ro-bind", str(kb_seeds_path), str(kb_seeds_path)]

    # Pre-built patient DB (single-kernel sweep): bind the parent dir read-only.
    if prebuilt_db_path is not None:
        bwrap += [
            "--ro-bind",
            str(prebuilt_db_path.parent),
            str(prebuilt_db_path.parent),
        ]

    # Pool mode: bind the whole sweep tmp dir so all per-patient DB files are
    # visible without relaunching anything per patient.
    if prebuilt_db_dir is not None:
        bwrap += ["--ro-bind", str(prebuilt_db_dir), str(prebuilt_db_dir)]

    # User namespace: needed so bwrap can bind-mount / set up the network
    # namespace as (mapped) root.  Nested inside the Apptainer instance's user
    # namespace, which HPC's AppArmor policy permits.
    bwrap += ["--unshare-user", "--uid", "0", "--gid", "0"]

    # OS-level network isolation when the host permits user network namespaces.
    # HPC sets max_net_namespaces=0 (nested too), so --unshare-net would fail
    # there; the Python socket guard remains the only network defense.
    if use_net_isolation:
        bwrap += ["--unshare-net"]

    # PID namespace so the kernel cannot enumerate/signal host PIDs; also makes
    # the kernel PID 1 in its own namespace.
    bwrap += ["--unshare-pid"]
    # Prevent the kernel from creating further user namespaces.
    bwrap += ["--disable-userns"]
    # Kill the kernel automatically if the wrapper dies.
    bwrap += ["--die-with-parent"]
    # CWD isolation: relative writes land in the private /tmp, not the host cwd.
    bwrap += ["--chdir", "/tmp"]

    # Environment — wipe the parent env (credentials, path hints) and restore
    # only what ipykernel strictly needs.
    bwrap += ["--clearenv"]
    bwrap += ["--setenv", "PATH", f"{_SANDBOX_VENV}/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"]
    bwrap += ["--setenv", "VIRTUAL_ENV", str(_SANDBOX_VENV)]
    bwrap += ["--setenv", "HOME", "/tmp"]
    bwrap += ["--setenv", "TMPDIR", "/tmp"]
    bwrap += ["--setenv", "PYTHONNOUSERSITE", "1"]
    bwrap += ["--setenv", "LANG", "C.UTF-8"]
    if uv_mode:
        # Running from /uv_python — the venv's site-packages are not on sys.path
        # automatically, so prepend them (plus the runtime dir for the guard).
        _py_ver = f"python{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}"
        _site_pkgs = str(_SANDBOX_VENV / "lib" / _py_ver / "site-packages")
        bwrap += ["--setenv", "PYTHONPATH", f"{_site_pkgs}:{runtime_dir}"]
    else:
        bwrap += ["--setenv", "PYTHONPATH", str(runtime_dir)]
    bwrap += ["--setenv", "JUPYTER_RUNTIME_DIR", str(runtime_dir)]
    # XDG dirs — keep caches inside the private /tmp.
    bwrap += ["--setenv", "XDG_CACHE_HOME", "/tmp/.cache"]
    bwrap += ["--setenv", "XDG_DATA_HOME", "/tmp/.local/share"]
    bwrap += ["--setenv", "XDG_CONFIG_HOME", "/tmp/.config"]
    bwrap += ["--setenv", "XDG_RUNTIME_DIR", "/tmp/runtime"]
    bwrap += ["--setenv", "MPLCONFIGDIR", "/tmp/.mpl"]

    # Per-kernel OpenMP / BLAS thread cap so concurrent sweep-pool kernels do not
    # oversubscribe the CPU (see _THREAD_LIMIT_ENV_VARS).
    if thread_limit is not None:
        for _thread_var in _THREAD_LIMIT_ENV_VARS:
            bwrap += ["--setenv", _thread_var, str(thread_limit)]

    # GPU / CUDA env vars — pass through so user-configured device selection and
    # library paths are respected inside the sandbox.
    for _gpu_var in (
        "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES",
        "NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES",
        "CUDA_HOME",
        "LD_LIBRARY_PATH",
    ):
        _gpu_val = os.environ.get(_gpu_var)
        if _gpu_val is not None:
            bwrap += ["--setenv", _gpu_var, _gpu_val]

    if dataset_path is not None:
        bwrap += ["--setenv", "HANCOCK_DATASET_PATH", str(dataset_path)]

    # Run bwrap inside the persistent instance: apptainer exec instance://<name>.
    # --cwd / because the instance is started with --no-mount cwd: the host cwd
    # does not exist inside the container, so without it Apptainer emits a
    # "Error changing the container working directory" warning on every exec.
    # Sets only bwrap's own cwd, which was previously an arbitrary fallback
    # ($HOME); the kernel's cwd stays /tmp via the inner --chdir. Every bind
    # path in the recipe is absolute, so no argument resolves against this.
    apptainer: list[str] = [
        "apptainer",
        "exec",
        "--cwd",
        "/",
        f"instance://{instance_name}",
    ]
    return apptainer + bwrap + launcher

"""
Stateful sandboxed Python kernel using jupyter_client.

Two-layer sandbox: one persistent Apptainer instance + per-kernel bubblewrap.

  * Apptainer instance (outer, started once):  ``apptainer instance start`` mounts
    the SIF a single time and holds a container namespace open for the whole
    process.  It is the "allowed to create namespaces" vehicle (on HPC,
    unprivileged bwrap is blocked by AppArmor, but bwrap nested *inside*
    Apptainer's user namespace is permitted) and a stable host-passthrough
    substrate (host /usr, /etc, /dev, the venv, uv-managed Python, and the temp
    root are bound in).  Instances are keyed by their stable data binds (dataset
    + KB paths); per-sweep DB dirs and per-kernel runtime dirs live under the
    bound temp root, so they are visible without changing the key.  Result: one
    instance per config, reused by every kernel, every sweep, and every pool
    refill — started lazily, stopped at process exit.

  * bubblewrap (inner, per kernel):  each kernel is launched as
    ``apptainer exec instance://<name> bwrap <recipe> python -m ipykernel``.
    bwrap builds the real per-kernel sandbox from the instance substrate — a
    private tmpfs /tmp, a fresh PID namespace, a read-only view of the venv and
    system libs, GPU device passthrough (``--dev-bind /dev/nvidia*``), and only
    the specific dataset / DB paths this kernel is allowed to see.  This is the
    proven pre-Apptainer recipe; because it re-isolates per kernel there is no
    cross-patient leakage even though kernels share the outer instance.

Transport is ZMQ over IPC (Unix-domain sockets in a bind-mounted runtime
directory) for every sandboxed kernel — no TCP loopback ports, so concurrent
kernel starts never race on a port.  The runtime directory is bound into bwrap
at its real host path, so a single connection file works inside and out.

OS-level network isolation (``--unshare-net``) is applied only where the host
permits user network namespaces (workstation); HPC disables them (NHR@FAU sets
/proc/sys/user/max_net_namespaces=0), so there the kernel shares the network
namespace and the Python socket guard (sitecustomize.py) is the only network
defense.  The interrupt path uses ``interrupt_mode = "message"`` (a ZMQ control
message) because bwrap's PID namespace makes the tracked PID the wrapper, not
the kernel, so a SIGINT would never reach ipykernel.

Set HANCAS_NO_SANDBOX=1 to skip isolation entirely (development only).
Apptainer must be on PATH and a SIF image must be available; run
./scripts/setup_sandbox.sh to install both.
"""

import asyncio
import logging

    _instances as _instances,

# Strip ANSI colour/reset codes from kernel tracebacks.
_ANSI_ESCAPE: Final = re.compile(r"\x1b\[[0-9;]*[mK]")

class KernelExecutor:
    """
    Persistent sandboxed Python kernel for interactive data analysis.

    Usage::

        executor = KernelExecutor()
        await executor.start()          # boots kernel, runs preamble
        output = await executor.execute("df_train.describe()")
        await executor.stop()

    The kernel is started lazily by :meth:`execute` if :meth:`start` has not
    been called explicitly.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._km: AsyncKernelManager | None = None
        self._kc: AsyncKernelClient | None = None
        self._started: bool = False
        self._kernel_tmp_dir: str | None = None
        self._kernel_runtime_dir: str | None = None
        self._last_start_timings: KernelStartTimings | None = None
        # Session id of the launched kernel wrapper, used in stop() to reap any
        # apptainer exec / bwrap helpers that linger (see _reap_sandbox_session).
        self._sandbox_sid: int | None = None

    @property
    def is_started(self) -> bool:
        """True once the kernel process is up and the preamble has run."""
        return self._started

    @property
    def last_start_timings(self) -> KernelStartTimings | None:
        """Timing breakdown from the most recent :meth:`start` call."""
        return self._last_start_timings

    async def start(
        self,
        preamble: str | None = None,
        dataset_path: Path | None = None,
        kb_models_path: Path | None = None,
        kb_functions_path: Path | None = None,
        prebuilt_db_path: Path | None = None,
        prebuilt_db_dir: Path | None = None,
        kb_seeds_path: Path | None = None,
        thread_limit: int | None = None,
        kb_models_readonly: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        """
        :param preamble: Optional Python code executed right after the kernel is
                         ready.  ``None`` by default — the kernel starts clean.
        :param thread_limit: When set, caps OpenMP/BLAS threads inside the kernel
                             (OMP_NUM_THREADS et al.) so concurrent pooled kernels
                             do not oversubscribe the CPU.  ``None`` leaves them
                             unset (backend default: one thread per core).
        :param dataset_path: When set, the dataset directory is bind-mounted
                             read-only into the sandbox (full file access).
                             When ``None``, the directory is excluded and
                             ``HANCOCK_DATASET_PATH`` is unset in the kernel env.
        :param kb_models_path: When set, the models directory is bind-mounted read-write into
                               the sandbox so the agent can persist trained ML model files there.
        :param kb_models_readonly: Bind the models directory read-only instead (sweep kernels:
                                   predict() only loads models, and anything it wrote there
                                   would be committed with the KB and seen by later sessions).
                                   Not enforced without a sandbox.
        :param kb_functions_path: When set, the functions directory is bind-mounted read-only
                                  into the sandbox so the agent can reload updated KB functions.
        :param prebuilt_db_path: When set, the parent directory of this pre-built patient DuckDB
                                 file is bind-mounted read-only.  Used by single-kernel sweep mode.
        :param prebuilt_db_dir: When set, this entire directory is bind-mounted read-only.
                                Used by pool mode.
        :param kb_seeds_path: When set, this directory is bind-mounted read-only as the seeds
                              directory so the synthesis agent can read all seed KBs.
        """
        _no_sandbox = os.environ.get("HANCAS_NO_SANDBOX", "0") not in ("", "0")

        if _no_sandbox:
            logger.info("Kernel sandbox: none (HANCAS_NO_SANDBOX)")
            sif_path: Path | None = None
        else:
            if shutil.which("apptainer") is None:
                raise KernelConfigError(
                    "Apptainer is required for kernel sandboxing but was not found on PATH.\n"
                    + "Run the setup script:\n"
                    + "  ./scripts/setup_sandbox.sh\n"
                    + "To skip isolation (development only): set HANCAS_NO_SANDBOX=1."
                )
            sif_path = _resolve_apptainer_sif()

        _sandboxed = sif_path is not None

        # Blocking filesystem calls below are run in a thread, not inline: this
        # coroutine can run on the same event loop as other concurrently-active
        # kernels (the sweep pool's background refill, in particular, starts a
        # replacement kernel while other kernels' predict()/cleanup calls are
        # still in flight on the same loop).  A synchronous mkdtemp/rmtree/write
        # that stalls on a contended host filesystem would otherwise freeze
        # message processing for every other kernel sharing the loop, making
        # them falsely appear unresponsive.
        # AF_UNIX socket paths are capped at 104-108 bytes depending on OS, so
        # this directory (holding only the tiny IPC connection file/sockets,
        # never large working data) needs to be short — macOS's default
        # TMPDIR (/var/folders/.../T/, ~40+ chars) alone leaves too little
        # room once the connection filename is appended. Pinned to bare /tmp
        # for that case. When sandboxed, tempfile.gettempdir() must be used
        # instead: _base_instance_binds() only bind-mounts that path (not
        # bare /tmp) into the Apptainer instance, and under Slurm it differs
        # from /tmp ($TMPDIR = /tmp/<jobid>, a sibling, not an ancestor) — a
        # hardcoded /tmp here would sit outside the instance's mounts, making
        # bwrap's bind of this dir fail with "Can't find source path" (the
        # cause of the tinyx job 1765161 failure). Linux $TMPDIR is always
        # short enough for the AF_UNIX limit, so this loses nothing there.
        _runtime_tmp_root = tempfile.gettempdir() if _sandboxed else "/tmp"
        self._kernel_runtime_dir = await asyncio.to_thread(
            tempfile.mkdtemp, prefix="hancas_kernel_runtime_", dir=_runtime_tmp_root
        )
        runtime_dir = Path(self._kernel_runtime_dir)
        _ = await asyncio.to_thread(_write_network_guard, runtime_dir)

        # Start (or reuse) the persistent Apptainer instance for this bind-set.
        instance_name: str | None = None
        connection_file_name: str = f"kernel-{uuid4()}.json"
        if _sandboxed:
            assert sif_path is not None
            # Install exit/SIGTERM cleanup here on the event-loop (main) thread —
            # the signal handler cannot be installed from the instance-start
            # worker thread below.
            _ensure_exit_cleanup_registered()
            # The KB working dirs are bound into the instance, so they must exist
            # before `apptainer instance start` (which fails on a missing mount
            # source).  The old per-kernel builder created these lazily; hoist it
            # here since the instance now starts first.  (The dataset and seeds
            # dirs must pre-exist and are not created.)
            def _mkdir_kb_dirs() -> None:
                for _kb_dir in (kb_models_path, kb_functions_path):
                    if _kb_dir is not None:
                        _kb_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

            await asyncio.to_thread(_mkdir_kb_dirs)
            data_binds = _instance_data_binds(
                dataset_path, kb_models_path, kb_functions_path, kb_seeds_path
            )
            handle = await asyncio.to_thread(
                _get_or_start_instance, sif_path, data_binds
            )
            instance_name = handle.name
            logger.info(
                "Kernel sandbox: instance %s + bwrap (%s)", instance_name, sif_path
            )

        km: AsyncKernelManager = AsyncKernelManager()

        # IPC transport over the private runtime dir, sandboxed or not: jupyter_client's
        # default TCP setup probes a free port, closes the probe socket, and hands the
        # bare port number to the newly-spawned kernel to bind later — a window where a
        # concurrently-starting kernel can grab the same port first. ipykernel's own
        # bind-retry logic (kernelapp.py's _bind_socket) only activates when the kernel
        # is free to pick its own port; since a specific number is always pinned here, a
        # collision is immediately fatal (zmq.error.ZMQError: Address already in use).
        # IPC sidesteps this with a private, guaranteed-unique named socket path instead
        # of a numbered port. For the sandboxed case, the runtime dir is bound at the
        # same real path inside bwrap, so one connection file works on both sides.
        km.transport = "ipc"
        km.connection_file = str(runtime_dir / connection_file_name)

        # jupyter_client 8.8+ builds the launch command from kernel_spec.argv.
        # Do NOT use km.kernel_cmd — that attribute is silently ignored in 8.8+,
        # which would start the kernel unsandboxed.
        kernel_spec = km.kernel_spec  # force-load the spec before mutation
        assert kernel_spec is not None
        kernel_spec.argv = _build_kernel_cmd(
            instance_name=instance_name,
            runtime_dir=runtime_dir if _sandboxed else None,
            connection_file_name=connection_file_name,
            dataset_path=dataset_path,
            kb_models_path=kb_models_path,
            kb_models_readonly=kb_models_readonly,
            kb_functions_path=kb_functions_path,
            kb_seeds_path=kb_seeds_path,
            prebuilt_db_path=prebuilt_db_path,
            prebuilt_db_dir=prebuilt_db_dir,
            use_net_isolation=_sandboxed and _max_net_namespaces() > 0,
            thread_limit=thread_limit,
        )

        if _sandboxed:
            # bwrap's --unshare-pid makes the tracked PID the wrapper, not the
            # kernel, so SIGINT (default "signal" mode) would never reach
            # ipykernel.  "message" sends interrupt_request on the ZMQ control
            # channel, which reaches ipykernel directly over the IPC socket.
            kernel_spec.interrupt_mode = "message"


        kernel_env: dict[str, str] | None = None
        if not _sandboxed:
            # Bare kernel (macOS or no sandbox): inherit host env but restrict
            # HANCOCK_DATASET_PATH and inject the Python-level network guard.
            self._kernel_tmp_dir = await asyncio.to_thread(
                tempfile.mkdtemp, prefix="hancas_kernel_"
            )
            kernel_env = {**os.environ, "TMPDIR": self._kernel_tmp_dir}
            if dataset_path is None:
                _ = kernel_env.pop("HANCOCK_DATASET_PATH", None)
            _existing_pp = kernel_env.get("PYTHONPATH", "")
            kernel_env["PYTHONPATH"] = (
                f"{runtime_dir}:{_existing_pp}" if _existing_pp else str(runtime_dir)
            )
            if thread_limit is not None:
                for _thread_var in _THREAD_LIMIT_ENV_VARS:
                    kernel_env[_thread_var] = str(thread_limit)

        start_kwargs: dict[str, object] = {"stdout": subprocess.DEVNULL}
        if kernel_env is not None:
            start_kwargs["env"] = kernel_env

        start_t0 = time.monotonic()
        launch_t0 = time.monotonic()
        await km.start_kernel(**start_kwargs)  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownMemberType]

        if _sandboxed:
            self._sandbox_sid = _read_sandbox_session_id(km)
            if self._sandbox_sid is not None:
                _active_sandbox_sids.add(self._sandbox_sid)
                _ensure_exit_cleanup_registered()
                _record_kernel_started()

        kc: AsyncKernelClient = km.client()
        kc.start_channels()
        # Assign km/kc before wait_for_ready so stop() can clean up if it times out.
        self._km = km
        self._kc = kc
        try:
            await kc.wait_for_ready(timeout=60)
            launch_seconds = time.monotonic() - launch_t0

            self._started = True
            logger.debug(
                "Kernel started (sandbox=%s).",
                "instance+bwrap" if _sandboxed else "none",
            )

            preamble_seconds = 0.0
            if preamble:
                preamble_t0 = time.monotonic()
                preamble_out = await self._collect(preamble, timeout=300.0)
                preamble_seconds = time.monotonic() - preamble_t0
                logger.debug("Preamble output:\n%s", preamble_out)
                if "__PREAMBLE_OK__" not in preamble_out:
                    if _KB_HOOK_IMPORT_FAILURE in preamble_out:
                        # Agent-fixable (a broken functions/*.py it wrote), not an
                        # infrastructure problem — a plain RuntimeError so callers
                        # (the tool-error fallback, the predict() validate-and-repair
                        # reprompt) can catch and act on it instead of it propagating
                        # as fatal like KernelConfigError does.
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            "KB function file(s) failed to import — fix the file(s) and "
                            + f"try again. Preamble output:\n{preamble_out}"
                        )
                    raise KernelConfigError(
                        "Kernel preamble failed: DuckDB setup did not complete. "
                        + "This usually means dataset files are missing or the dataset path is not "
                        + "mounted into the sandbox (duckdb_preamble implies mount). "
                        + f"Preamble output:\n{preamble_out}"
                    )
        except Exception:
            await self.stop()
            raise

        self._last_start_timings = KernelStartTimings(
            launch_seconds=launch_seconds,
            preamble_seconds=preamble_seconds,
            total_seconds=time.monotonic() - start_t0,
        )

    async def execute(
        self,
        code: str,
        timeout: float = 300.0,
        interrupt_idle_timeout: float = 30.0,
    ) -> str:
        """
        Execute Python code and return combined stdout / result / error text.

        Starts the kernel lazily if not yet started.

        :param code: Arbitrary Python source code.
        :param timeout: Maximum seconds to wait for completion.
        :param interrupt_idle_timeout: Seconds to wait for the interrupted kernel
            to return to idle after a timeout.
        :return: Plain-text output (stdout, repr, or traceback).
        """
        if not self._started:
            await self.start()
        return await self._collect(
            code, timeout=timeout, interrupt_idle_timeout=interrupt_idle_timeout
        )

    async def stop(self) -> None:
        """Shut down the kernel process and release every descriptor it holds.

        Descriptor hygiene here is critical: the sweep pool discards and replaces
        kernels continuously, and jupyter frees the manager's ZMQ context /
        control socket / ipc files only as the *final* step of a *successful*
        ``shutdown_kernel``.  A kernel wedged in a non-interruptible call makes
        that shutdown hang, so we (1) bound the graceful shutdown so it cannot
        hang, (2) force-run jupyter's own resource cleanup when the shutdown did
        not complete, and (3) unconditionally destroy the *client's* context,
        which jupyter never closes.  Skipping any of these leaks descriptors per
        discard and eventually crashes the run with "Too many open files".

        ``shutdown_kernel`` kills only the kernel's process group; any lingering
        ``apptainer exec``/``bwrap`` wrappers are reaped explicitly via the
        kernel session id.  The persistent Apptainer instance is left running
        (shared across kernels) and torn down at process exit.
        """
        km = self._km
        kc = self._kc
        self._km = None
        self._kc = None

        try:
            if km is not None:
                # Bounded graceful shutdown.  On success jupyter runs its own
                # cleanup_resources; on a wedged kernel this hangs and is cut off
                # by the timeout (or the pool's stop backstop cancelling us).
                await asyncio.wait_for(
                    km.shutdown_kernel(now=True),  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownMemberType, reportUnknownArgumentType]
                    timeout=_KERNEL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT,
                )
        except Exception:
            logger.debug("Graceful kernel shutdown did not complete.", exc_info=True)
        finally:
            # Release descriptors unconditionally and synchronously.  Runs even
            # if the shutdown above hung and this coroutine is being cancelled:
            # closing sockets/contexts needs no await, so it completes.  Both are
            # idempotent after a successful shutdown.
            _release_manager_fds(km)
            _release_client_fds(kc)

        if self._sandbox_sid is not None:
            sid = self._sandbox_sid
            self._sandbox_sid = None
            _active_sandbox_sids.discard(sid)
            try:
                await asyncio.to_thread(_reap_sandbox_session, sid)
            except Exception:
                logger.debug(
                    "Kernel session reap failed for sid=%s.", sid, exc_info=True
                )
            # Verify the reap cleared the session.  Survivors here are stuck in
            # an uninterruptible (D-state) kernel/driver call that even SIGKILL
            # cannot reap until it returns — the GPU-wedge signature.
            try:
                survivors = await asyncio.to_thread(_session_pids, sid)
            except Exception:
                survivors = []
            if survivors:
                _record_kernel_stopped(clean=False)
                logger.warning(
                    "Kernel session %s left %d process(es) alive after reap "
                    + "(likely wedged in a non-interruptible GPU/driver call): pids=%s",
                    sid,
                    len(survivors),
